newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-PARK PITCHES DODGERS INTO FIRST PLACE TIE.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-PARK PITCHES DODGERS INTO FIRST PLACE TIE.

text.p: Chan Ho Park turned in his best performance of the season on Thursday to lead the surging Los Angeles Dodgers past the reeling Chicago Cubs.

Park (10-5) scattered three hits over eight-plus innings for his fifth straight win and Raul Mondesi had three hits and two RBI as the Dodgers moved into a first-place tie in the NL West with a 4-1 win over the Cubs.
Park, who gave up one run with two walks and seven strikeouts, retired 19 consecutive batters during a dominating stretch before issuing a leadoff walk to Sammy Sosa in the bottom of the ninth.
"I thought Park pitched his best game of the year," Dodgers manager Bill Russell said. "I would have liked to have let him finish, but after the walk to Sosa, I thought that he had had it."
Todd Worrell finished up to notch his 27th save as the Cubs suffered their eighth consecutive loss.

Mondesi had an RBI fielder's choice in a two-run first inning against Terry Mulholland (6-11), and added his 23rd homer in the sixth for Los Angeles, which tied the San Francisco Giants with a 59-49 record.
"It's the longest home run I've hit this year, I don't think there's any question about it," Mondesi said.
At Florida, Tony Saunders combined with three relievers on a four-hitter and Darren Daulton's RBI single accounted for the scoring as the Marlins edged the first-place Atlanta Braves 1-0.

Saunders (3-3) allowed four hits over seven innings, walked four and struck out seven for his third win in as many starts gainst Atlanta this season. Robb Nen retired four straight batters to record his 100th career save.

Edgar Renteria had two hits and scored the only run as the Marlins beat the Braves for the seventh time in their last eight meetings to move within 5 1/2 games of first-place Atlanta in the NL East and one game in front of the New York Mets in the wild card race.
In Montreal, Rondell White collected three hits, including a solo homer, and four RBI and Chris Widger added a three-run shot as the Expos pounded the San Diego Padres 9-2.

White opened the scoring in the first with a homer off Sterling Hitchcock (7-6) and added a three-run double in the second, extending Montreal's lead to 6-0. White is 6-for-6 with three homers and seven RBI lifetime against Hitchcock.
Dustin Hermanson (5-5) allowing two runs and seven hits over six innings with seven strikeouts for the Expos, who have won five of six meetings with San Diego this season.

In Philadelphia, Midre Cummings's bases-loaded single scored Gregg Jefferies in the bottom of the 10th inning as the Phillies nipped the St Louis Cardinals 2-1 to match their longest winning streak of the year at three.
Ricky Bottalico (2-3) worked the 10th to get the win in relief of Curt Schilling, who struck out 11 and allowed four hits and three walks over nine innings.
St Louis reliever Tony Fossas (1-3) took the loss after starter Matt Morris scattered six hits over seven innings and allowed just one run.
In Pittsburgh, Jason Schmidt scattered six hits over eight innings and Kevin Young hit a three-run homer in the eighth to lift the Pirates to a 4-1 win over the Colorado Rockies.
Schmidt (6-6) allowed a home run to Larry Walker in the sixth inning, walked four and struck out five. Rich Loiselle struck out the side in the ninth for his 16th save.

Colorado starter Roger Bailey (9-8) gave up a run-scoring double to Jermaine Allensworth that tied the game 1-1 in the eighth. Curtis Leskanic came in to face Young, who sent a 3-2 pitch over the right-field fence for his 15th homer.
